title: A ray in water meeting the surface
caption: Going from water (n = 1.33) to air the ray bends away from the normal. The critical angle is sin θ_c = 1/1.33, θ_c = 48.8°. At 45°, below θ_c, the ray escapes at sin⁻¹(1.33 sin 45°) = 70°; at 60° it is above θ_c and is totally reflected.
alt: Two ray diagrams at a water–air surface: a ray at 45° leaves into the air at 70° from the normal, and a ray at 60° is totally internally reflected.
description: The lesson's ray in water (n = 1.33) hits the surface at 45°. The critical angle is sin⁻¹(1/1.33) = 48.8°.
45° is less than 48.8°, so the ray escapes, bending away from the normal to 70°: n₁ sin 45° = n₂ sin r.
A second ray at 60° is greater than the critical angle: nothing escapes and the ray is totally internally reflected.
